title_as_printed: Resolving Heterogeneity in the Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease and its Progression Using Multimodal Data

Task_Type.reason: Unsupervised similarity network fusion + spectral clustering to discover subtypes; core results are two MCI subtypes compared on biomarkers, longitudinal decline, Kaplan-Meier and Cox models. No supervised classifier is trained; the ~90% 'accuracy' is cluster-to-diagnosis agreement.
Task_Type.quote: we successfully identified two MCI subtypes with biological and clinical significance, validated by longitudinal studies of cognitive, clinical, fluid biomarkers and MRI-related features

Category.reason: The fused network is built from three co-equal input modalities: neuropsychological scores (C5: ADAS, RAVLT, mPACC, LDELTOTAL, TRABSCOR, FAQ), genetics (C3: APOE status and polygenic hazard score only) and structural MRI volumes (C1: seven volumes). The registry lists only C3, omitting two primary input domains (MRI and neuropsych), which carry most of the between-cluster differences. Blood gene expression (GSVA) and CSF add further C3 support; PET is used only for validation.
Category.quote: First, we constructed a similarity network for subjects using cognitive scores, genetics, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) related data, respectively.

Validation_Type.reason: No supervised predictive model; leave-one-out is used only to test cluster stability (n = 972, so V1 would not apply anyway); external validation is listed as future work.
Validation_Type.quote: larger cohorts and validation in independent external datasets (e.g., NACC, AIBL) are essential to enhance the reliability and robustness of the findings.

Sample_N_Approx.quote: Our study was based on 972 subjects with at least four years of follow-up information. At baseline, 37 of these individuals were diagnosed with AD, 565 with MCI, and 370 with cognitively normal (CN).

Publication_Year.reason: Journal of Molecular Neuroscience (2026) 76:24; received 4 Sep 2025, accepted 9 Jan 2026.

ADNI_Dependent.quote: Data used in this work were obtained from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) database

notes: Category undercount removes this multimodal study from the neuroimaging (C1) and clinical/neuropsych (C5) domain tallies. is_model_study=false is borderline: the study is unsupervised subtyping whose reported 'accuracy' (100% present AD, ~88% future AD) is cluster-to-diagnosis agreement, not validated classification; it is correctly coded T4/V2 so it should not enter the classification-only validation statistics.
